content_fit_flags: Big Mac Index should be framed as a useful PPP illustration, not a complete currency valuation model.
Working-hours comparisons offer a strong reader-centered alternative to dollar prices.
A basket or median is more robust than a single consumer product.
Lipstick Index is better presented as a media-friendly hypothesis than a dependable predictor.
Men’s Underwear Index has memorable branding but weak formal evidence.
Baltic Dry Index provides stronger economic grounding than the folklore indicator family.
Cigarette-equivalent pollution must be labeled as a risk analogy, not literal chemical-dose equivalence.
PM2.5, AQI, annual exposure and short-term spikes must not be collapsed into one measure.
Indices can lose integrity when institutions optimize directly for the measured number.
AI benchmarks and readiness rankings fit as a modern index family, even when not classical economic indices.

package_notes.risk: The cigarette comparison can mislead if presented as literal equivalence; PM2.5, AQI, annual exposure and short-term spikes must remain distinct. CO2 flight equivalents may broaden the package but dilute the core.
package_notes.strength: Distinctive, highly legible hook connecting pollution to an everyday unit; supported by the corpus’s explicit risk-analogy framing and measurement caveats.

package_notes.risk: Breadth may feel arbitrary without a clear organizing principle; several candidate indices are explicitly weakly evidenced or better treated as hypotheses.
package_notes.strength: Broadest range of memorable indicators, with a strong built-in myth-versus-measurement tension and room to contrast weak folklore signals with more grounded measures such as the Baltic Dry Index.

package_notes.risk: The central index is described as memorable but weakly evidenced, limiting authority and potentially narrowing the package’s scope.
package_notes.strength: Memorable title with immediate curiosity and a clear debunking angle; can anchor discussion of formal evidence versus cultural folklore.

package_notes.risk: Lipstick and men’s underwear are both vulnerable to the corpus’s reliability cautions; the title may imply stronger macroeconomic validity than the evidence supports.
package_notes.strength: Commercially vivid combination of familiar objects; supports a clear progression from Big Mac PPP illustration to basket-based measurement and skepticism about folklore indicators.

package_notes.risk: The package spans consumer prices, affordability and environmental exposure, so it needs a disciplined method to avoid becoming a collection of analogies rather than a coherent index story.
package_notes.strength: Strong reader-access proposition: hours, meals, rent, phones and pollution translate abstractions into lived experience. The corpus directly supports working hours and strange-but-familiar units as explanatory devices.

package_notes.risk: The range is conceptually broad and may require stronger framing to connect classical economic signals with AI indices and benchmark culture.
package_notes.strength: Supports a modern, wide-angle narrative across freight, electricity, reservations and AI; combines physical-economy indicators with emerging benchmark and readiness rankings.

work_replaced: manual clustering sanity check over already-normalized corpus; final ranking remains Codex/human judgment
